title: Shingled LPDDR staircase on glass panel replaces TSV stacks
idea: Box: 1T1C LPDDR die x planar access x on-die SA x offset-staircase edge pads x glass-core panel x panel-level RDL. Eight LPDDR dies are shingled with 0.4 mm offsets so every die's edge pads stay exposed, then a single panel-level RDL plus through-glass vias wires all eight to a 1024-bit bus without one TSV.
why: HBM TSV tax (fact 6): no TSV keep-out area and no 20-30% stack yield loss; uses commodity LPDDR wafers at roughly half the wafer area per bit of HBM, at about half HBM's bandwidth density.

title: Bridge-resident row cache absorbs DRAM activations near GPU
idea: Box: 1T1C DRAM x standard access x on-DRAM SA x hybrid-bonded silicon bridge x Si bridge chiplet x 7 nm logic. The EMIB-style bridge between GPU and DRAM carries 64 MB of SRAM that holds whole recently opened 2 KB rows, fed through a 2 um-pitch hybrid bond so a full row moves for ~0.05 pJ/bit; re-hits are served from the bridge and the row is never re-activated.
why: Destructive read and overfetch (fact 8), row hammer (fact 9): 3-5x fewer activations on AI streams with reuse, random-read energy from ~5.9 to ~1.5 pJ per useful bit, and hammer patterns starve.

title: MicroLED imaging-fiber links make cheap DDR act like HBM
idea: Box: commodity DDR5 die x standard access x standard SA x 300-lane microLED/CMOS-photodiode array x coherent imaging fiber bundle x flip-chip GaN-on-Si chiplet. Each lane is a blue microLED at ~2 Gb/s imaged pixel-to-pixel through the bundle, so a buffer chip next to commodity DRAM delivers HBM-class aggregate bandwidth at <1 pJ/bit over 1-5 m.
why: Data movement (fact 5) and HBM TSV tax (fact 6): substitutes DDR (about 1/3 the wafer area per bit of HBM) for HBM while keeping bandwidth, and lets memory live outside the hot package.

title: Sub-terahertz waveguides inside glass core link memory chiplets
idea: Box: HBM-lite stack x standard x standard x 300 GHz on-die patch launchers x glass-core substrate with laser-written dielectric waveguides x panel process. Instead of thousands of interposer wires, 32 sub-THz channels at 100 Gb/s each ride rectangular waveguides formed inside the package glass core, so memory can sit 20-50 mm from logic.
why: Interposer cost and shoreline: removes the 2.5D silicon interposer and decouples memory count from logic perimeter, targeting ~1 pJ/bit with 3-4x more attachable stacks.

title: Interposer made of DRAM: memory inside the substrate
idea: Box: planar 1T1C at relaxed F~25 nm x planar access x local SA x face-to-face hybrid bond x the interposer itself x DUV-only fab. The 2.5D interposer, today dead silicon, is fabricated as a reticle-stitched DRAM array with routing channels, and GPU/CPU chiplets hybrid-bond on top so each chiplet reads the gigabytes directly beneath it.
why: Capital intensity (fact 4) and data movement (fact 5): DUV-only node with zero EUV layers, reuses area already paid for, ~0.1 pJ/bit vertical access, ~10-20 GB per 2,500 mm2 interposer.

title: Per-bitline hybrid bonds move all sense amps to logic
idea: Box: vertical-channel 1T1C array x VCT access x sense amplifiers on 5 nm logic wafer x 0.8 um-pitch Cu-Cu bonds per bitline pair x Si x wafer-to-wafer bonding. The memory wafer becomes ~95% array because every bitline pair lands on its own bond pad and is sensed, decoded and repaired on a separate logic wafer stacked face-to-face.
why: Periphery 49% of die (fact 7): roughly doubles bits per memory-wafer area and puts periphery on fast logic transistors, also shortening the data path to ~0.1 pJ/bit.

title: Capacitive proximity coupling makes memory tiles reworkable, not bonded
idea: Box: 1T1C DRAM tile x standard access x charge-domain receiver x capacitive pads at 15 um pitch across a 1 um gap x spring-clamped Si carrier x no bump, no bond. Memory tiles are clamped face-down over the logic chip's pad field and talk through capacitive coupling, so a failing tile is unclipped and swapped instead of scrapping a $30k package.
why: HBM yield loss (fact 6): known-good package becomes field-replaceable, recovering the 20-30% stack and assembly scrap and allowing graded tiles; link ~0.2 pJ/bit.

title: Fluidic self-assembly drops tiny DRAM dielets into panel wells
idea: Box: 0.5 mm2 DRAM dielets x standard x on-dielet SA x shape-keyed wells plus panel RDL x 600 mm organic panel x fluidic self-assembly. Asymmetric trapezoid dielets tumble in a carrier fluid until they lock into matching wells, then one RDL pass wires thousands of dielets into wide memory channels.
why: Yield and assembly capital: tiny dies yield >95% even at aggressive rules, and parallel assembly replaces millions of pick-and-place moves; cost per good bit -15-25%.

title: Wavelength-addressed banks: the address is the light colour
idea: Box: 1T1C sub-arrays x wordline fired by a ring-filter photodiode x bitline read by microring modulator x WDM bus x SiN waveguides deposited below 400 C on DRAM BEOL x back-end photonics. Each bank owns one wavelength; a request is a pulse at that colour that only its filter absorbs, firing the wordline with no global row/column decoder tree, and data returns on a modulated carrier.
why: Periphery (fact 7) and data movement (fact 5): removes much of the global decode and long electrical I/O; speculative ~30% die-area saving and <1 pJ/bit off-die.

title: Backside power mesh halves HBM through-silicon via count
idea: Box: HBM DRAM x standard x standard x front-side signal-only hybrid bonds plus backside nano-TSV power grid x thinned Si x backside-power flow borrowed from logic. Power and ground, about half of HBM's TSVs, move to a backside metal mesh fed by dense 0.5 um nano-TSVs, so only signal TSVs remain in the keep-out zone.
why: TSV tax (fact 6): ~40-50% fewer large TSVs, ~3-5% die area recovered, and lower IR drop that permits taller stacks.

title: Defective DRAM arrays recycled as flying capacitors for regulators
idea: Box: failed 1T1C sub-arrays x wordlines held on x no sensing (capacitor bank) x in-stack switched-capacitor converter x each DRAM die x fuse-programmed at test. Sub-arrays that fail test are fused into parallel banks (5 fF x millions = tens of nF) that act as flying caps for an on-die 4:1 converter, so the stack accepts 4 V input on far fewer power TSVs.
why: Yield and TSV tax (fact 6): turns scrap area into function, cuts power TSVs and bumps ~4x through higher input voltage, and lowers I2R loss.

title: Memory dies stand on edge like books on logic
idea: Box: DRAM die x standard x standard x sidewall-metallized edge bond at 20 um pitch x logic die as the shelf x laser-patterned sidewall plating. Thin DRAM dies are diced, edge-metallized and stood vertically in rows on the base logic die, so stack height no longer limits die count and each die's top edge touches the cold plate.
why: TSV tax and thermal ceiling of tall stacks: zero TSVs, 32+ dies per footprint row each with a direct heat path; bandwidth scales with edge length.

title: Uncut wafer-scale DRAM slab with redundancy routing fabric
idea: Box: 1T1C DRAM x standard x standard x on-wafer mesh network with spare-tile routing x whole 300 mm wafer x no dicing. The entire DRAM wafer serves as one memory, with a reconfigurable mesh that routes around bad tiles, face-to-face bonded to a wafer-scale compute or optical I/O wafer.
why: Packaging cost and data movement: no dicing, bumping or per-die packaging; ~1-2 TB per wafer at ~0.3 pJ/bit; yield handled by redundancy instead of scrap.

title: Sense amplifiers double as 100 mV interposer link receivers
idea: Box: DRAM x standard x cross-coupled latch receiver x 100 mV-swing interposer wires treated as long bitlines x Si interposer x standard fab. The interface reuses the DRAM's own sense-amp latch topology as a clocked receiver, so the transmitter only dumps a small charge on the wire, like a cell sharing charge with a bitline.
why: Interface energy (fact 5) and voltage floor (fact 10): CV2 at ~0.1 V swing gives ~10x less link energy, HBM I/O from ~1 pJ toward 0.1-0.2 pJ/bit.

title: Sense-amp XOR delta encoding transmits only flipped bits
idea: Box: DRAM x standard x SA with XOR against a shadow latch holding the last-sent word x transition-coded TSVs x Si x standard. Each column remembers what it last sent; the SA outputs the XOR so a wire toggles only when a bit changed, and the receiver re-integrates.
why: Data movement energy: switching activity on correlated AI tensor streams falls 40-60%, cutting TSV and interposer I/O energy proportionally.

title: Infrared light crosses thinned silicon instead of TSVs
idea: Box: DRAM x standard x Ge photodiode receivers x 1310 nm micro-emitter arrays shining vertically through the dies x thinned Si (transparent at 1.3 um) x no via etch. Signals cross the stack as light through the silicon bulk while power uses a few large peripheral vias.
why: TSV tax (fact 6): removes signal TSV keep-out area and TSV process steps; ~0.5 pJ/bit if emitters are efficient enough.

title: Memory scroll: dielets on flex coiled around the processor
idea: Box: DRAM dielets x standard x standard x fine-line polyimide ribbon x flexible substrate x roll-to-roll assembly. Dielets are bonded along a 2 m flex ribbon that coils around the processor package like a scroll, so attachable memory grows with the number of turns instead of the die's shoreline.
why: HBM shoreline limit: 3-5x more attachable capacity per package at DDR-like cost per bit.

title: Charge-sharing pooled reads send sums, not raw bytes
idea: Box: 1T1C x multi-wordline activation x analog charge sharing across N cells digitized by an ADC in the base die x TSV x Si x standard. Activating several cells on one bitline averages their charge into an analog sum the base die digitizes, so pooling, attention accumulation or Bloom-filter reductions ship one value instead of N.
why: Data movement: 4-16x fewer bits across TSVs and package for reduction-heavy AI kernels.

title: Boron-arsenide interlayers let HBM stacks grow to 24 dies
idea: Box: HBM die x standard x standard x hybrid bond with 2 um cubic BAs or CVD-diamond interlayers plus thermal vias x Si x low-temperature deposition. Ultra-high-conductivity interlayers spread heat sideways to dedicated thermal through-vias so 24-high stacks stay under 85 C.
why: Bits per package footprint: +50% capacity per stack site without new shoreline; cooler dies also need less refresh.

title: Secondary-market DDR4 reborn in CXL memory expansion boxes
idea: Box: reclaimed DDR4 DIMMs x standard x standard x CXL controller with per-rank ECC remap and aging-aware refresh x refurbished chassis x refurbishment line. DDR4 from decommissioned servers is tested, graded and re-hosted behind CXL controllers that hide its latency for tier-2 data.
why: Supply: capacity with zero new wafers; tens of PB of DDR4 retire each year; cost per GB ~20-30% of new DDR5.

title: Logic on top, memory beneath through dedicated power columns
idea: Box: DRAM stack x standard x standard x power columns through reserved DRAM zones plus face-to-face signal bonds x DRAM as base x hybrid bonding. The accelerator die sits on top of the DRAM stack, next to the cold plate, and the DRAM below carries dedicated power-via columns, putting every compute tile ~50 um from its memory.
why: Data movement (fact 5) and HBM shoreline: ~0.1 pJ/bit with bandwidth set by area rather than die edge; DRAM runs warmer, offset by temperature-aware refresh.

title: Liquid-nitrogen memory packages kill refresh and wire resistance
idea: Box: 1T1C x cryo-optimized high-Vt access x SA retuned for 77 K x copper interposer at 77 K x cryostat-integrated package x standard fab. At 77 K access-transistor leakage falls by orders of magnitude so retention stretches from 64 ms to hours, and copper resistance drops ~6x so links run at lower swing.
why: Refresh (fact 3) and data movement (fact 5): near-zero refresh energy and bandwidth loss, ~3x cheaper wires; cryo-cooling overhead partly offsets.

title: Pulse-position DRAM I/O encodes three bits per edge
idea: Box: DRAM x standard x time-to-digital receiver x pulse-position-modulated TSV and interposer lanes x Si x standard. Each lane sends one edge per unit interval whose position among eight timing slots encodes 3 bits, so wires toggle 3x less often for the same data.
why: I/O energy (fact 5): ~2-3x lower switching energy per bit at modest TDC area cost.

title: Laser-sliced active layers replace backgrinding and save donor wafers
idea: Box: HBM DRAM x standard x standard x hybrid-bond stack x reusable donor wafer x dry laser subsurface slicing. A laser-focused cleave plane 40 um under the device layer lets the finished DRAM layer split off dry, skipping water-cooled backgrinding and polish; the remaining wafer is plasma-smoothed and reused for another DRAM layer.
why: Water: backgrind/polish coolant and rinses are a top packaging water draw; dry cleave plus plasma cuts that >10x. Also cuts virgin silicon and quartz-crucible demand (Spruce Pine chokepoint) by reusing donors 5-10x.

title: Diamond fly-cut planarization enables CMP-free hybrid bonding
idea: Box: DRAM x standard x standard x Cu-Cu surface-activated bonding x Si x single-point diamond fly-cutting plus Ar fast-atom-beam activation in vacuum. Bond surfaces are flattened by dry ultra-precision fly-cutting and activated in UHV, eliminating CMP slurry, post-CMP scrubbing and DI rinses.
why: Water: CMP and post-CMP cleans are among the largest UPW users in hybrid bonding; the dry route cuts >10x and removes slurry chemistry supply.

title: Inductively coupled stack powered wirelessly: no TSV, no plating
idea: Box: DRAM x standard x on-die coil receivers x inductive data links plus resonant wireless power through 15 um dies x dry-plasma-thinned Si x laminated dry-film adhesive stack. Dies are glued with dry film, data crosses via coil pairs and power via a per-die resonant transformer, so TSV etch, Cu plating, CMP and their rinses disappear.
why: Water and TSV tax (fact 6): removes every wet TSV step, ~10-20x less water per stack, and recovers TSV keep-out area; power-transfer efficiency is the risk.

title: Laser-forward-transferred copper redistribution on glass, no plating bath
idea: Box: LPDDR dies x standard x standard x fan-out RDL x glass panel x laser-induced forward transfer (LIFT) of Cu nanoparticle ink plus laser sintering. 8-15 um RDL lines are written digitally from a donor ribbon and sintered in place, replacing resist coat/develop, seed sputter, electroplating, strip and etch and the rinse after each.
why: Water: semi-additive plating lines use hundreds of litres per panel; dry digital additive writing cuts >10x and maskless writing removes photomasks.

title: Photonic wire bonds written in place link memory and compute
idea: Box: DRAM chiplet with SiN grating couplers x standard x Ge photodiodes x free-form polymer waveguides x organic carrier x two-photon direct laser writing with closed-loop recycled solvent developer. 3D polymer waveguides are written in situ between memory and compute chiplets after placement, so no interposer and no active optical alignment are needed.
why: Water: eliminates silicon-interposer fabrication (many wet clean and plating loops) for ~10x less water per package; ~1 pJ/bit over centimetres.

title: Mirror lid reflects free-space light between memory and logic
idea: Box: DRAM chiplet x standard x photodiode array x upward-facing microLED arrays bounced off a molded aspheric mirror lid x dry-laminated power-only carrier x injection molding. Chiplets need only a few power layers below; all memory data travels as light up to the lid and back down to the processor.
why: Water: removes the interposer and high-layer-count signal substrate (the wet-heavy parts), ~10x less water; bandwidth no longer tied to shoreline.

title: Extruded polymer waveguides replace water-hungry memory PCB traces
idea: Box: DDR/LPDDR modules x standard x standard x 140 GHz CMOS transceivers into PTFE dielectric waveguide cables x extruded polymer x dry extrusion. Memory channels leave the motherboard entirely as 100 Gb/s mm-wave links through plastic waveguides, so boards shrink from 20+ to ~8 layers.
why: Water: every PCB layer pair adds wet etch, plating and rinse; memory-channel interconnect water falls >10x when plated layers become extruded cable; also enables memory at rack distance.

title: Aligned-particle conductive film attaches memory without flux or washing
idea: Box: DRAM die x standard x standard x anisotropic conductive film with magnetically aligned Ni-Au particles at 10 um pitch x organic or glass substrate x dry thermocompression. One press bonds the die, forms the underfill and makes every contact, eliminating flux, aqueous post-reflow wash and capillary underfill.
why: Water: flux cleaning and underfill prep dominate die-attach water; ACF is dry, >10x less water, and faster.

title: Supercritical-CO2 electroplating fills TSVs with no rinse steps
idea: Box: HBM DRAM x standard x standard x Cu TSV x Si x electroplating in a supercritical CO2/electrolyte emulsion. The low-viscosity emulsion penetrates high-aspect TSVs void-free and depressurizes to leave wafers dry, so the multi-stage DI rinses and spin-dries vanish; CO2 is recompressed and reused.
why: Water: plating plus rinse is a large share of TSV water, cut >10x; better high-aspect fill also lifts stack yield (fact 6).

title: Monolithic gain-cell memory in logic BEOL using dry steps only
idea: Box: 2T0C gain cell x ALD In2O3 channel transistors x current sensing in logic FEOL x monolithic BEOL integration x the logic wafer x ALD, plasma etch and vapor-HF cleans only. Memory layers are deposited above the compute inside its interconnect stack: no separate DRAM wafer, no dicing, no thinning, no package-level memory link.
why: Water: the separate DRAM fab and packaging water disappear and the added BEOL steps are dry, >10x less per GB; data movement drops to ~0.05 pJ/bit.

title: Elastomer stamps mass-transfer memory dielets dry, microLED-style
idea: Box: 0.3 mm DRAM dielets x standard x standard x transfer-printed onto RDL x panel x laser release from carrier plus kinetically controlled PDMS stamp mass transfer. Borrowed from microLED fabs, one stamp stroke picks up 10,000 dielets and prints them onto the panel.
why: Water: replaces water-sprayed blade dicing and wet release with laser release and dry transfer, >10x cut; small dielets raise yield and allow fine-grained memory placement.

title: Hot remote memory sleds rejecting heat through dry air coolers
idea: Box: DRAM or gain cell with retention tuned for 105 C x standard x standard x optical CXL link x air-cooled sled x standard. Memory moves out of liquid-cooled accelerator packages into separate sleds running at 45 C inlet, cooled by dry coolers with no evaporative towers.
why: Water: evaporative data-center cooling (~1.8 L/kWh) for memory heat goes to ~0, >10x cut per memory-watt; needs hot-tolerant refresh policy.

title: Single vacuum cluster: plasma-dice, CO2-snow clean, activate, bond
idea: Box: HBM DRAM x standard x standard x die-to-wafer hybrid bond x Si x integrated vacuum cluster with plasma dicing, CO2-snow particle removal and plasma activation. Wafers enter once and leave as bonded stacks; dies never touch water or room air, so no pre-bond DI clean is needed.
why: Water: removes dicing water, megasonic cleans and rinses (>10x); particle-free surfaces also raise hybrid-bond yield against the HBM yield loss (fact 6).

title: Copper wires ultrasonically embedded in thermoplastic form the interposer
idea: Box: LPDDR or HBM-lite x standard x standard x wire-scribed routing x hot-embossed thermoplastic carrier x ultrasonic embedding of 15 um insulated Cu wire. A CNC head lays and embeds insulated wires into the polymer like a multiwire board, with laser-ablated ends forming pads: no etch, no plating, no rinse.
why: Water: substrate fabrication is packaging's main water user; wire scribing is dry, >10x less, and yields an ultra-cheap carrier for memory-dense packages.

title: Dry-grown carbon nanotube forests as compliant memory interconnects
idea: Box: DRAM x standard x standard x CNT-forest bumps densified and metal-capped x Si x dry thermal CVD growth plus ALD metal cap. Compliant CNT pillars absorb +/-1 um topography, so dies stack without CMP flattening, plating or solder flux.
why: Water: removes CMP, plating and flux wash (>10x); compliance tolerates thin-die warpage; contact resistance is the risk.

title: Dry-developed metal-oxide resist patterns all redistribution layers
idea: Box: DRAM chiplets x standard x standard x fan-out RDL x Si or glass x vapor-deposited tin-oxide resist with plasma dry development and dry metal etch. Every lithography step in the RDL/interposer flow runs with no spin coat, aqueous develop or wet strip.
why: Water: develop, strip and rinse are a major litho water draw; dry resist plus dry etch cuts >10x for RDL layers and resist chemical use ~5x.

title: Molten-salt ion exchange writes waveguides inside glass interposers
idea: Box: DRAM chiplets with grating couplers x standard x photodiodes x buried graded-index waveguides x glass interposer x dry molten KNO3/AgNO3 ion exchange through a laser-ablated metal mask. Waveguides form by ion exchange in a molten salt bath, with no water anywhere, and carry memory traffic across the package.
why: Water: replaces wet silicon-interposer processing, >10x less; optical package links at <1 pJ/bit.

title: Magnetic self-alignment snaps dielets into place on vibrating tables
idea: Box: DRAM dielets with patterned NiFe pads x standard x standard x self-aligned direct bonding x substrate with matching micromagnets x dry vibratory assembly. Dielets scattered on the substrate are pulled into +/-0.5 um registration by magnetic forces and then bonded, with no liquid (unlike capillary or fluidic assembly).
why: Water: dry self-assembly replaces fluidic/capillary methods and post-placement wet cleans, >10x cut; enables low-cost massive-dielet memory.

title: Laser-debonded HBM reclaimed from retired accelerators and remounted
idea: Box: used HBM3 stacks x existing x existing x laser debond, laser solder-jet re-bump, remount on new carrier x reclaimed package x dry laser rework. Retired GPU modules have their HBM stacks lifted by IR laser heating, tested, re-balled with jetted solder spheres and reused on inference cards.
why: Water: a reused stack needs zero fab water (vs thousands of litres per wafer), >100x cut per reused GB; adds supply with no new wafers.

title: Shingled overlap: memory die hangs over logic die edge
idea: Box: DRAM die x standard x standard x 2 mm overlap strip bonded face-to-face by Cu-Sn transient-liquid-phase thermocompression x no interposer x dry formic-acid-vapor oxide reduction. The memory die extends over the logic die's edge so a 2 mm strip of each faces the other, forming a direct bridge with no interposer or bridge chip.
why: Water: deletes the wet-heavy interposer and uses fluxless dry bonding, >10x cut; links ~0.2 pJ/bit.

title: CHIPS packaging grants gated on litres-per-gigabyte water budgets
idea: Box: any memory x any access x any sensing x any packaging route x U.S. sites x dry toolsets required. Federal packaging incentives require metered packaging water intensity of 0.1 L/GB or less, with bonus credit for dry steps such as laser dicing, SAB, ACF and dry resist.
why: Water and U.S. manufacturability: lets packaging plants get permits in water-stressed Arizona and Texas, forces 10x cuts and creates a U.S. market for dry tools.

title: Dry-pack foundry business for water-stressed U.S. regions
idea: Box: customer memory dies x any x any x SAB, ACF or inductive stacking x glass or thermoplastic carriers x laser, plasma and dry-film steps only. A U.S. contract packager built with no UPW plant at all, offering memory stacking where wet fabs cannot get water rights, on cheaper land with faster permits.
why: Capital and U.S. manufacturability: skips $100M+ UPW and wastewater plants, ~10-20x less water, and saves years of permitting.

title: Flash-resident KV cache with attention-guided prefetch over CXL
idea: Box: dense 3D NAND x standard x standard x CXL/optical link with predictive prefetch engine x SSD x standard. The LLM KV cache lives on flash; a small predictor in the controller uses top-k attention scores to prefetch the token blocks the next step needs into a 10x smaller DRAM buffer.
why: Water and DRAM demand: ~10x less DRAM per served session; NAND needs far less fab water per bit, so memory water per session falls ~10x.
